issue_context.title: Viewer does not support local files on Chromium
issue_context.body:
Configuration:
- Web browser and its version: QtWebEngine 5.12 (Chromium 69), Chrome 72
- Operating system and its version: Windows 7
- PDF.js version: 2.0.943, 2.1.266
- Is a browser extension: No

Steps to reproduce the problem:
1. Open viewer locally (file:///C:/pdftest/web/viewer.html)

What is the expected behavior? 

Embedded PDF shown (it works in Firefox ESR 60).

What went wrong? 

Error in console: Fetch API cannot load file:///C:/pdftest/web/compressed.tracemonkey-pldi-09.pdf. URL scheme must be "http" or "https" for CORS request.

I have seen #9361 and #9020 but I don't think that's the solution in this case.
comments:
As is clearly mentioned in the README, see https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js#getting-the-code, not all browsers support the `file://` protocol:

> Finally, you need to start a local web server as some browsers do not allow opening PDF files using a `file://` URL.

Chrome supports the file protocol, as it works with the built-in PDF viewer and with the chrome extension (which was apparently fixed in https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/pull/9363). So I'm pretty sure this is a bug in pdf.js and not a missing feature in Chrome.

`fetch` with file:// doesn't work in Firefox either (just try `fetch("file:///C:/pdftest/web/compressed.tracemonkey-pldi-09.pdf"` in console). So there must be a slightly difference opening the viewer in Firefox and on Chrome.

review_comments: Is there a reason why we don't use a polyfill for `fetch` instead of having manual fallback logic? Since it's not too much code I don't really have a strong preference, but it looks like `babel-preset-env` can do this (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/44908044/babel-not-polyfilling-fetch-when-using-babel-preset-env) and there is also https://github.com/github/fetch.

Given the (somewhat) advanced usage of `fetch` found in https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/master/src/display/fetch_stream.js it's not clear to me if a polyfill would generally work well.

The main reason for *not* attempting to polyfill though, is that as you can see in the added checks `fetch` only works for the `http`/`https` protocols, whereas `XMLHttpRequest` can work for e.g. the `file`/`ftp`/... protocols as well.
Could you add a unit test for this new utility function?
That's a fair point, will fix this.
